raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Stacked on https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61303 (its commit is the first of the two here; review the second commit).

After `sleep(level=2)` discards the weights pool, `reload_weights` on a ModelOpt NVFP4 MoE model (GLM-5.2-NVFP4, FlashInfer TRT-LLM backend, MLA) brings the server back healthy and serving garbage: well-formed completions, wrong content. Two independent causes, fixed behind env flags so the default path is unchanged:

- `VLLM_RELOAD_KEEP_MOE_KERNEL=1`: on reload, keep the ModelOpt NVFP4 MoE kernel the CUDA graphs were captured with and copy the freshly derived quant-config tensors into the ones it references, instead of building a new kernel.
- `VLLM_LAYERWISE_RELOAD_MEASURED_TOTALS=1`: trigger a layer's layerwise processing from the element count its loaders reported during the first load, not from the declared parameter sizes, and process a ready layer only once a load for another layer arrives.

## Claims

- With both flags, after `wake_up` + `reload_weights` every parameter, buffer and derived tensor hashes identical to a fresh load. Measured on vLLM **0.20.2** (this PR is the port to `main`): 10 rounds out of 10 on 4x TP=2 GLM-5.2-NVFP4 on an 8xB300, content-verified completions; without the fixes, 0 of 10.
- Reload through the pinned Run:ai path (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61303): 113 s → 55 s per TP=2 pair.
- This is what makes a GPU-state snapshot (CRIU + cuda-checkpoint) of a *sleeping* server usable: a 17 GB image per TP=2 pair instead of 491 GB, with the weights refilled from one page-cached copy of the checkpoint.

## Validation

- New CPU unit test `test_layerwise_reload_measured_first_load_totals` in `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py`: a layer whose scale loader is called twice per expert (so its loaders report 8 elements where the layer declares 6), streamed with the over-counted parameter last. With the stock trigger the layer is processed two loads early and a tensor derived in `process_weights_after_loading` stays stale (`[222, 0]`); with the measured total it is correct (`[222, 242]`). Both variants run and pass; the rest of `test_reload.py` that runs on CPU still passes (38 passed, the remaining cases need the GPU fixtures).
- `pre-commit` `ruff-check`, `ruff-format`, `typos` pass on the changed files.
- **Not yet re-run on hardware against `main`.** The 10/10 result is from the same two fixes applied to 0.20.2. Parts of the 0.20.2 patch are already upstream and were dropped from this port: #48251 (MLA `W_UV`/`W_UK_T` refreshed in place), #49489 (shared NVFP4 MoE scales writable, which also removes the need for an overlap-tolerant copy), #40390 (`replace_parameter(prefer_copy=True)`), #59158 (KV-init runtime state offloaded on sleep). I will re-run the wake+reload checksum drill on `main` as soon as I have the node again and post here; draft until then.

## Details

**Cause 1, stale derived tensors.** `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoE._build_moe_kernel` runs on every `process_weights_after_loading`, so a reload builds a new `FusedMoEQuantConfig` and kernel. The activation gscales (`a1`/`a2`) in that config are derived at load time and are not layer parameters, so the layerwise reload's copy into kernel tensors does not cover them: the captured graphs keep pointers to the old tensors, whose memory the level-2 sleep discarded. Eager steps use the new tensors, graph replays the stale ones. The fix keeps the kernel on reload and refreshes its quant-config tensors in place (`_refresh_moe_quant_config_inplace`, per-descriptor, same shape/dtype/device required, otherwise rebind with a warning). The new kernel's `fused_experts.process_weights_after_loading(layer)` still runs so the layer's parameters are converted; the layerwise machinery then copies them back into their original storage as before.

**Cause 2, early trigger.** The layerwise reload processes a layer once `load_numel >= get_layer_size(layer)`. NVFP4 MoE scale loaders are called more than once per parameter (one call per expert per projection), and the Run:ai streamer yields tensors out of file order, so the count reaches the declared size before the last scale tensors have arrived; the layer is quantized early and the trailing loads are dropped as "Excessive loading" (the `Limitations(4)` case in `layerwise.py`). The per-call cap in `get_numel_loaded` cannot see repeated calls. `record_first_load_numel(model)` wraps every weight loader during the first `load_weights` (only when the flag is set), records the per-layer total in `LayerReloadingInfo.first_load_numel` (kept across `reset()`), and `initialize_online_processing` uses it as `load_numel_total` when reloading. As a second line of defence a ready layer is processed only when a load for another layer arrives (`PENDING_LAYERS`), flushed in `finalize_layerwise_processing`.

Both are opt-in because they have been validated on one model family and one backend; if maintainers would rather have the measured-total trigger on by default, I am happy to drop the flag.

---

@@ -82,6 +82,14 @@ vllm serve /home/meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct \
     --model-loader-extra-config '{"memory_limit":5368709120}'
 ```
 
+You can set `pinned_staging` to page-lock the streamer's CPU buffer and have the streamer copy every tensor to the GPU out of it, so the host-to-device copies run as DMA copies from pinned memory instead of pageable copies. This helps on hosts where the weight load is bound by the copy path rather than by storage (for example a large checkpoint on a fast local disk or a parallel filesystem). The buffer is registered once per load, at roughly 0.2 s per GB, so unless `memory_limit` is set it is bounded to 16 GB. If the buffer cannot be pinned, loading falls back to the regular path.
+
+```bash
+vllm serve /home/meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct \
+    --load-format runai_streamer \
+    --model-loader-extra-config '{"pinned_staging":true}'
+```
+
 !!! note
     For further instructions about tunable parameters and additional parameters configurable through environment variables, read the [Environment Variables Documentation](https://github.com/run-ai/runai-model-streamer/blob/master/docs/src/env-vars.md).

+        assert os.environ["RUNAI_STREAMER_MEMORY_LIMIT"] == "1024"
+
+    with patch.dict(os.environ, {"RUNAI_STREAMER_MEMORY_LIMIT": "2048"}, clear=False):
+        _runai_loader({"pinned_staging": True})
+        assert os.environ["RUNAI_STREAMER_MEMORY_LIMIT"] == "2048"

+class _DerivingQuantMethod(QuantizeMethodBase):
+    """Derives a tensor from the layer's scale when processing runs, the way
+    quant methods derive kernel scales; stale if processing ran too early."""
+
+    uses_meta_device = True
+
+    def create_weights(self, layer, *weight_args, **extra_weight_attrs):

+
+    def apply(self, layer, *args, **kwargs):
+        raise NotImplementedError
+
+    def process_weights_after_loading(self, layer):
+        layer.scale_doubled = layer.scale.detach().clone() * 2
+
+
+class _OverCountingScaleLayer(torch.nn.Module):
+    """A layer whose per-expert scale loader is called twice per expert (one
+    call per projection), so its loaders report more elements than the layer
+    declares, like NVFP4 MoE expert scales."""
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.weight = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(2, 2))
+        self.weight.weight_loader = default_weight_loader
+        self.scale = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(2))
+        self.scale.weight_loader = _OverCountingScaleLayer.scale_loader
+        self.quant_method = _DerivingQuantMethod()
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def scale_loader(param: torch.Tensor, loaded_weight: torch.Tensor, expert_id: int):
+        param.data[expert_id].copy_(loaded_weight)
+
+
+class _OverCountingScaleModel(torch.nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.layer = _OverCountingScaleLayer()
+
+    def load_weights(self, weights):
+        for name, loaded_weight, *extra in weights:
+            param = getattr(self.layer, name)
+            param.weight_loader(param, loaded_weight, *extra)
+
+
+def _over_counting_weights(base: float):
+    # The over-counted parameter is streamed last, so the declared-size
+    # trigger fires two loads early and the trailing expert scale is dropped.
+    return [
+        ("weight", torch.full((2, 2), base)),
+        ("scale", torch.tensor(base + 10.0), 0),
+        ("scale", torch.tensor(base + 11.0), 0),
+        ("scale", torch.tensor(base + 20.0), 1),
+        ("scale", torch.tensor(base + 21.0), 1),
+    ]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("measured_totals", [False, True])
+def test_layerwise_reload_measured_first_load_totals(monkeypatch, measured_totals):
+    monkeypatch.setattr(envs, "VLLM_LAYERWISE_RELOAD_MEASURED_TOTALS", measured_totals)
+    reload_layerwise.PENDING_LAYERS.clear()
+    model = _OverCountingScaleModel()
+    layer = model.layer
+
+    with record_first_load_numel(model):

+    assert torch.equal(layer.scale_doubled, torch.tensor([24.0, 44.0]))
+    # loaders are restored and the measured count (4 + 4 calls of 1) is kept
+    assert layer.scale.weight_loader is _OverCountingScaleLayer.scale_loader
+    assert layer.weight.weight_loader is default_weight_loader

+
+    kernel_scale = layer.scale
+    record_metadata_for_reloading(model)
+    initialize_layerwise_reload(model)
+    expected_total = 8 if measured_totals else 6
+    assert get_layerwise_info(layer).load_numel_total == expected_total
+    model.load_weights(_over_counting_weights(100.0))
+    finalize_layerwise_reload(model, SimpleNamespace(dtype=torch.float32))
+
+    assert layer.scale is kernel_scale

+    assert torch.equal(layer.scale, torch.tensor([111.0, 121.0]))
+    if measured_totals:

+    else:

+        # layer is processed before the second expert's scale arrives
+        assert torch.equal(layer.scale_doubled, torch.tensor([222.0, 0.0]))

+def _refresh_moe_quant_config_inplace(
+    dst: FusedMoEQuantConfig, src: FusedMoEQuantConfig

+    """Copy every tensor of ``src`` into the tensor ``dst`` holds in its place.

+    Used on weight reload so the quant config captured by CUDA graphs keeps

+    refreshed in place; it is rebound with a warning, and captured graphs

+        dst_desc = getattr(dst, desc_name)

+# 0.2 s/GB once per load; 16 GB keeps that to a few seconds while leaving the

+RUNAI_PINNED_STAGING_DEFAULT_BYTES = 16_000_000_000
+# Threads used to pre-fault the staging buffer before it is page-locked.

+def _pin_runai_streamer_buffer(streamer) -> int | None:
+    """Page-lock the Run:ai streamer's CPU staging buffer.
+
+    The streamer reads every tensor into one reusable host buffer and the
+    host-to-device copies out of it run as pageable copies, i.e. a driver
+    staged memcpy per tensor. Registering the buffer with ``cudaHostRegister``
+    turns those into DMA copies out of pinned memory. The pages are faulted in
+    with ``MADV_POPULATE_WRITE`` from several threads first, so the
+    single-threaded registration does not pay for the page faults itself.
+
+    Returns the registered address, to be passed to ``cudaHostUnregister``
+    once the iterator is exhausted, or ``None`` if the buffer could not be
+    pinned. In that case loading continues unchanged on the pageable path.
+    """
+    try:
+        buf = streamer.file_streamer.file_streamer.requests_iterator.buffer
+    except AttributeError as e:
+        logger.warning(
+            "Run:ai streamer staging buffer not found (%s); "
+            "loading from pageable memory.",
+            e,
+        )
+        return None
+    nbytes = int(buf.nbytes)
+    if nbytes == 0:
+        return None
+    addr = int(buf.ctypes.data)
+    start_time = time.perf_counter()
+    try:
+        import ctypes
+
+        libc = ctypes.CDLL("libc.so.6", use_errno=True)
+        page = 4096
+        madv_hugepage = 14  # MADV_HUGEPAGE
+        madv_populate_write = 23  # MADV_POPULATE_WRITE, Linux >= 5.14
+        begin = addr & ~(page - 1)
+        end = (addr + nbytes + page - 1) & ~(page - 1)
+        libc.madvise(
+            ctypes.c_void_p(begin), ctypes.c_size_t(end - begin), madv_hugepage
+        )
+        step = (end - begin) // _RUNAI_PINNED_STAGING_TOUCH_THREADS
+        step = max((step + page - 1) & ~(page - 1), page)

+            )

+            for lo in range(begin, end, step)

+        for thread in threads:
